prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Meet Your Desktop Companion!", "Learn how to easily summon, hide, and interact with your pet on your desktop."]
1: ["Checking Desktop Compatibility", "We are verifying screen settings to ensure your desktop pet renders cleanly."]
2: ["Your Pet is Being Created!", "While you wait, explore quick mini-activities to learn how to care for your pet."]
3: []
4: ["Sign In to Save Your Pet", "Log in to link your pet to your account and keep progress synced across sessions.", "Use your primary account so your pet data is safely backed up."]
5: ["Generating Your Pet", "Assembling 3D animations and desktop behaviors..."]
6: ["Official Adoption Certificate", "Congratulations! Your new companion is officially adopted and ready for setup."]
7: ["Choose Your Companion", "Preview pet behaviors and animations side-by-side to make your choice."]
8: ["Your Pet is Ready on Desktop!", "Enable system tray shortcuts so your pet is always accessible with one click."]
9: ["Upload Pet Photos", "For the best render, use clear, well-lit photos facing forward.", "Avoid dark or blurry images so your pet model renders cleanly."]
